theory.overview: Dynamic Programming (DP) is an algorithmic paradigm that solves complex problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems, solving each subproblem only once, and storing their solutions (memoization) for future use. Key characteristics are: Optimal Substructure (optimal solution contains optimal subsolutions) and Overlapping Subproblems (same subproblems recur). DP approaches include top-down memoization (recursive) and bottom-up tabulation (iterative). DP is essential for optimization problems like knapsack, longest common subsequence, and edit distance.

keyConcepts.name: Optimal Substructure
keyConcepts.description: Optimal solution to the problem can be constructed from optimal solutions to its subproblems. A prerequisite for DP.

keyConcepts.name: Overlapping Subproblems
keyConcepts.description: Same subproblems are solved multiple times in naive recursion. DP stores results to avoid recomputation.

keyConcepts.name: Memoization (Top-Down)
keyConcepts.description: Recursive approach that stores computed results in a table. Natural to write, uses call stack.

keyConcepts.name: Tabulation (Bottom-Up)
keyConcepts.description: Iterative approach that fills table from base cases up. More space efficient, no recursion overhead.

complexity.space: O(states) can often optimize to O(states) or less

problems.title: Best Time to Buy/Sell Stock with Cooldown

algorithmSteps.description: Fibonacci: fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2), base cases fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1
Naive: fib(5) calls fib(4) and fib(3). fib(4) calls fib(3) and fib(2). Overlapping!
Memoization: Store fib(2)=1, reuse instead of recomputing.
Bottom-up: dp[0]=0, dp[1]=1. Fill: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2].
Space optimized: Only need last 2 values. O(1) space!
Result: fib(5) = 5. Computed in O(n) time with memoization.
